newsitem.title: USA: Mobil rolling out Speedpass gasoline system.
newsitem.headline: Mobil rolling out Speedpass gasoline system.

text.p: In another case of No. 2 trying harder, Mobil Corp. is rolling out what it says will be a faster way for Americans to buy gasoline.
Mobil, the nation's second largest gasoline marketer, said it was introducing a technology called Speedpass in nine major cities across the country this weekend.
But the nation's largest gasoline marketer, Shell Oil, is already testing special pumps in San Diego.
Customers enrolled in the Mobil Speedpass programme will simply wave a miniature electronic device attached to their key chain in front of designated gasoline pumps.
They will then be able to gas up immediately and drive away without opening their wallets or purses for credit cards or cash.

People living in the nine metropolitan areas -- in and around Boston, Washington, D.C., Orlando, Miami and Tampa, Fla., Detroit, Chicago, Los Angeles and San Diego -- are hearing all about it on their radio and TV stations.

That is where Mobil is running advertisements created by DDB Needham in a campaign that includes billboard ads and ads in major newspapers. Meanwhile, Shell is getting ready to test similar technology it calls Easy Pass this summer.
